intro: Nine short beats. Each is also a presenter note. Use the arrow keys in presenter mode to step the diagram on screen. The story under each beat is told about {{cast.company}} and its {{cast.assistantWord}}, {{cast.assistant}}; pick another vertical on the Stories tab to retell it.

On the hosted copy (the banner says so), say it plainly: direction 2 is simulated by the lab's teaching server, direction 1 uses real PingFederate, and state is ephemeral, lost on restart, and kept per visitor, so Reset clears only your own workspace.

beats.title: 1. The registration problem
points: A {{cast.clientWord}} that wants to use an {{cast.serverWord}} has to register with it first.
Every server keeps a record per {{cast.clientWord}}, and every {{cast.clientWord}} repeats this for every server.

beats.title: 2. The idea
points: Let the {{cast.clientWord}}'s id be an https URL.
The {{cast.serverWord}} fetches the JSON document behind the URL and reads the {{cast.clientWord}}'s settings from it.
Show the Learn tab, DCR versus CIMD diagram, and press Simulate.

beats.title: 3. What is in the document
points: client_id equals the URL itself, plus redirect_uris, a name, and no secret.
Point at the field list on the Learn tab.

beats.title: 4. Why the server is strict
points: A stranger chooses the URL, so the {{cast.serverWord}} must bound what it fetches.
Walk the rules list: https, URL equals source, listed redirect addresses, no secrets, no private addresses.

beats.title: 5. Direction 1: PingFederate as the server
points: Open the PingFederate as server tab. The lab is the {{cast.clientWord}}, PingFederate is the {{cast.serverWord}}.
This part uses real PingFederate. There is no mock of it.
Say plainly: whether PingFederate can act as a CIMD client is not verified, and the lab does not claim it.

beats.title: 6. Reading the probe
points: Tick the confirm box and run the probe only when the owner has PingFederate ready.
Accepted means PingFederate fetched and validated the document and moved on to sign-in.
HTTP 400 means no enabled CIMD policy matches that URL. PingFederate takes one metadata URL per policy.

beats.title: 7. Direction 2: the lab as the server
points: Open the Lab as server tab and run the tester.
This is a teaching server, not a product. The table shows one good document and each way a document goes wrong.
Expand a row to show the raw request, response and traceparent.

beats.title: 8. Refusals are the point
points: Mismatched id, a published secret, an oversize document, a redirect, a private address: each is refused at a named check.
Show the summary line, then the full flow where a second use of the code fails.

beats.title: 9. Close
points: CIMD removes the registration step but moves trust to the document and to the server's fetch rules.
Press Reset to clear your workspace on the lab and restore the diagrams, ready for the next audience.
